text:
Piece Puzzle · 4-player individual match

1. Objective
Each player uses the same eight Pieces in five types to complete a grid of four rows crossing four columns.
Compete for your own survival. The first 3 players to submit a completed puzzle survive, and the last 1 is eliminated for good.
Each player works on their own board in private, without conversation, negotiation, or relationship reviews.

2. Notches and orientation
Each Piece has 4 notches. side 0 is a notch cut from the top, and side 1 is a notch cut from the bottom.
depth is the notch depth when the Piece height is taken as 100, and is one of 33, 58, or 83.
The two notches at each crossing must face opposite sides, top and bottom, and their depths must sum to at least 100.
Read the notches on row Pieces from left to right, and on column Pieces from top to bottom.
reverse=true reverses the notch order, and flip=true swaps the top and bottom directions of every notch.

3. Gameplay
Each turn, everyone simultaneously and privately chooses one action: place, remove, submit with the buzzer, or pass.
When placing a Piece, specify a position from 1 to 4 in a horizontal row or vertical col. You may reposition a Piece already on the board.
If another Piece occupies the chosen slot, it returns to the tray. Only a placed Piece can be removed.
Specify the final position and orientation for the Piece. The notch conditions at the crossings determine whether it fits.
Even with all 8 Pieces placed and all 16 crossings fitting, you must press the buzzer with submit to submit a completed puzzle.
After an incorrect submission, you can adjust your board and submit again.

4. Rankings
Players who submit a completed puzzle on an earlier turn rank higher. Ties on the same turn are decided by the draw order announced at the start.
The game ends once three survivors are determined, and all final boards are revealed. You cannot see other players' boards during the game.
Once the model-call limit is reached, play continues with scripted default actions. Malformed model actions are treated as passes.

The existing crossing is valid at 33+83. Placing K5 in row 2 also gives opposite notch sides at its crossing with K1, with a combined depth of 116. The remaining crossings have not yet been checked.

P09 checked that retaining the three existing rows and placing K5 in reverse in row 4 allows all crossings to be matched with the four remaining Pieces. P09 will keep adding Pieces without changes, aiming for the earliest completed submission.
Both existing crossings are valid. Placing K3 flipped in column 2 also satisfies the crossing conditions in rows 1 and 2.
Both existing crossings fit. Placing K3 flipped in column 2 makes both new crossings fit, and the remaining Pieces can complete the grid.

The two existing crossings are valid, but keeping K4 and K5 as they are leaves no Piece that can fit column 4. Moving K5 with a flip to row 3 fits the existing column and allows row 2 to be chosen again.

P09 confirms that placing K7 flipped in column 1 makes the directions and depths fit at all four crossings. The remaining K6, K8, and K4 also fit in columns 2, 3, and 4, respectively, so continue toward completion without corrections.
All four existing crossings are valid. Placing K4 flipped in row 2 preserves both crossings and frees K5 for another slot.
All four existing crossings are correct. Placing K2 with reverse and flip in column 4 also makes its two crossings fit, with depth sums of 166 and 116.
Both existing crossings are valid. Placing K8 in column 4 gives depths of 33+83 in row 1 and 58+58 in row 3, with opposite directions at both crossings.

P09 has confirmed that placing K6 in column 2 in its original orientation gives opposite notch sides at all four crossings, with combined depths of at least 100. Continue placing without spending turns on revisions, aiming for an early completed submission.

All four existing crossings are valid. Placing K5 with reverse and flip in column 4 makes the two new crossings fit as well, but the arrangement will need further adjustments to complete the puzzle with the remaining Pieces.

All 6 current crossings fit, but the remaining Pieces cannot complete the puzzle while preserving the existing arrangement. Replacing column 4 with K7 allows the remaining three Pieces to be placed to complete it.
All four existing crossings are valid. Placing K2 flipped in row 2 makes both crossings fit, and the remaining K6, K3, and K7 can fill the other slots.

P09 confirmed that placing K8 in its original orientation in column 3 satisfies both the direction and depth conditions at all four crossings. This keeps the shortest path on track: place K4 in column 4 next turn, then submit.
The existing crossing at row 2, column 4 does not fit and needs correction. Placing K8 reversed in row 4 makes all crossings with the three current columns fit.
All six existing crossings fit, and placing K8 flipped in row 3 also makes the three new crossings fit. Whether the remaining placements can complete the grid still needs to be checked.
All six existing crossings are valid. Placing K6 in column 1 fits the three rows, and the remaining K3 and K7 can fill the empty positions.

P09 confirms that placing K4 in column 4 in its original orientation gives opposite directions and depth sums of at least 100 at all four remaining crossings. Complete the arrangement this turn, then press the buzzer next turn to try to survive.
Row 2, column 4 currently does not fit. Placing K7 reversed and flipped in column 4 makes all three existing crossings fit and frees K5 for reuse.
All 9 current crossings fit. Placing K5 in column 3 also makes the 3 new crossings fit, but the remaining K2 cannot go straight into row 4, so further adjustments are needed.
All 9 existing crossings are valid. Placing K3 flipped in column 3 makes three crossings fit, and K7 can then be placed flipped in row 4 next turn.
P09 has confirmed that all eight Pieces are placed and all 16 crossings fit, with no errors. Submit immediately to secure the earliest completion rank and survival.
All 9 current crossings fit. Placing K5 with a flip in row 2 preserves its three valid crossings and makes it possible to use K4 in the remaining position.
All 12 existing crossings on P10's board fit. Placing K2 in row 4 creates two mismatches, so a later adjustment is needed.
All 12 existing crossings are valid. Placing K7 flipped in row 4 gives opposite notch sides at all four crossings, with combined depths of at least 100.
All 9 current crossings fit. Placing K6 in column 3 makes two of its three new crossings fit, but the row 4 crossing will need correcting later.

All eight Pieces are placed and all 16 crossings are valid, so submitting immediately gives a better chance of survival.
